metadata.note: The Atlantic and St. Lawrence Railroad's own passenger operation, 1848-1853: the US half of the Portland - Montreal line, opened from Portland in stages (Yarmouth 1848, Danville Junction 1848, Mechanic Falls 1849, Oxford 1849, South Paris 1850, Bethel 1851, Gorham 1851, Northumberland 1852, Island Pond 1853) and run by the A&StL until the Grand Trunk's 999-year lease took effect 1 Jul 1853. Each feature is the leg opened at one stage, drawn from its opening year to 1853, so in any year the drawn legs add up to Portland - the then-terminus. From 1853 the same track is drawn by grand_trunk_railway_montreal_portland.geojson (Grand Trunk 1853-1923, Canadian National 1923-1967). After 1853 the A&StL existed only as a lessor and ran no trains.

metadata.geometry_method: No new tracing: every feature is a slice of the existing OSM-traced grand-trunk-montreal-portland geometry, cut at that feature's already-checked station mileposts (Northumberland at the nearest point to Groveton).
not_yet_sourced: Stage opening months for Yarmouth, Danville Junction, Mechanic Falls, Oxford, South Paris, Bethel and Northumberland rest on one uncited secondary source (Wikipedia, St. Lawrence and Atlantic Railroad). Poor's 1860 History of the Railroads and Canals, the A&StL annual reports (Bowdoin) or Portland newspapers would confirm them.
Passenger carriage on the stages before Gorham is inferred from 'opened' on a common-carrier line; no timetable or notice naming passenger trains in 1848-1850 was found.
Oxford: Sept 1849 is 'construction to Oxford', not an explicit opening; the conservative start is 1850.
Whether the 1848-53 alignment differs from the surviving traced route, especially at the Portland terminal.
Headway before Feb 1853 and all speeds are estimates.
source_conflicts: Portland - Yarmouth opening day: 20 Jul 1848 (Wikipedia) vs 4 Jul 1848 (unidentified snippet). Year unaffected.
Gorham opening day: 22 Jul 1851 (Wikipedia, Gorham station) vs 23 Jul 1851 (Wikipedia, St. Lawrence and Atlantic Railroad). Year unaffected.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: None: the A&StL had no branches, and its Portland wharf trackage carried no passenger trains.

segments.note: First section of John A. Poor's Portland - Montreal line, opened July 1848 (20 Jul per Wikipedia; a 4 Jul date also circulates and is probably a conflation with the 4 Jul 1846 ground-breaking). Passenger carriage in 1848 is inferred from the opening of a common-carrier railroad; no 1848 timetable or notice was found. Drawn to 1853 because the Grand Trunk's 999-year lease took effect 1 Jul 1853 (indenture signed 5 Aug 1853); the A&StL ran its own trains until then and only collected rent afterwards. 1853 is therefore drawn both here and on the Grand Trunk feature, as the repo does at every ownership change. headway_min 720 is the A&StL's own Feb 1853 timetable (two passenger trains each way daily over the whole line), applied back to earlier years as an ESTIMATE; avg_speed_kmh is an estimate. Neither is sourced for 1848-1852.

segments.note: Opened to Gorham NH 22 or 23 July 1851 (the two Wikipedia articles disagree on the day). The best-evidenced stage for passengers: the A&StL built the White Mountain Station House at Gorham for the first trains, making Gorham the White Mountains' tourist gateway, and its own 1851 petition to the Vermont legislature says the road was 'in operation' for 91 miles, Portland to Gorham. Drawn to 1853 because the Grand Trunk's 999-year lease took effect 1 Jul 1853 (indenture signed 5 Aug 1853); the A&StL ran its own trains until then and only collected rent afterwards. 1853 is therefore drawn both here and on the Grand Trunk feature, as the repo does at every ownership change. headway_min 720 is the A&StL's own Feb 1853 timetable (two passenger trains each way daily over the whole line), applied back to earlier years as an ESTIMATE; avg_speed_kmh is an estimate. segments.note: Completed to Island Pond VT 29 January 1853. The A&StL's own Winter Arrangement of 1 Feb 1853 runs two passenger trains each way daily Portland - Island Pond under the A&StL name, the firmest primary evidence that the company ran passenger trains itself. Its own operation of this leg lasted only until the July 1853 lease, so at year resolution this leg adds nothing to 1853 except the operator: the Grand Trunk feature already draws the same track that year. Drawn to 1853 because the Grand Trunk's 999-year lease took effect 1 Jul 1853 (indenture signed 5 Aug 1853); the A&StL ran its own trains until then and only collected rent afterwards. 1853 is therefore drawn both here and on the Grand Trunk feature, as the repo does at every ownership change. headway_min 720 is the A&StL's own Feb 1853 timetable (two passenger trains each way daily over the whole line), applied back to earlier years as an ESTIMATE; avg_speed_kmh is an estimate.
